rules.title: An SNMP community entry carries a name or an index from the dictionary of trivial community strings.
rules.remediation: Remove the community entry with configure snmp delete community or configure snmpv3 delete community, and where SNMP is needed replace it with an SNMPv3 user that authenticates.
refs: ExtremeXOS v33.7.1 Command References, chapter Commands: configure snmp add community
ExtremeXOS v33.7.1 Command References, chapter Commands: configure snmpv3 add community
rules.known_false_positives: The finding never carries the community, only which field of the entry matched and that the value is in the dictionary; the dictionary holds public and private and the comparison ignores letter case, so a community that differs from one of them by case alone is reported too. The rule reads the two forms 33.7.1 documents, configure snmp add community and configure snmpv3 add community, and it reads the plain value: an entry written with the hex or the encrypted keyword is not compared at all. Whether a switch that still carries the community entries of its factory state prints them into show configuration has not been measured against a device with this code, so a device left at those defaults may yield no finding rather than one. Version 2 derives the object key from a SHA-256 digest of the tokenized object identity (SNMP access mode and community, or SNMPv3 community index). Reordering or inserting unrelated entries does not change it. The digest is an identifier, not encryption. Version 1 ordinal identities cannot be mapped safely without their original configuration; review and recreate affected baselines and suppressions from a new report.

rules.title: The switch accepts Telnet, which carries the password of the session in clear text.
rules.remediation: Send disable telnet and reach the switch over SSH, which EXOS enables with enable ssh2.
refs: ExtremeXOS v33.7.1 Command References, chapter Commands: enable telnet
ExtremeXOS v33.7.1 Command References, chapter Commands: disable telnet
rules.known_false_positives: Telnet is enabled by default in 33.7.1 (both the enable telnet and the disable telnet entry state Default: Enabled), so a configuration that names neither command is reported with the reason default enabled; a dump that reached the tool truncated before the telnetd module is therefore reported as well. The two commands are read as a flat sequence and the last one wins, which is how a list of imperative commands is applied; a configuration carrying both has not been seen. The rule says nothing about who may reach the open port: a switch that leaves Telnet enabled and blocks it in an access-list zone is reported just the same, because those entries are not read.

rules.title: The switch sends its log to no remote syslog collector.
rules.remediation: Add a collector with configure syslog add and turn the remote export on with enable syslog.
refs: ExtremeXOS v33.7.1 Command References, chapter Commands: configure syslog add
ExtremeXOS v33.7.1 Command References, chapter Commands: enable syslog
rules.known_false_positives: Remote logging needs two things in 33.7.1 - a target from configure syslog add and the export turned on with enable syslog, whose entry states Default: Disabled - but enable syslog does not appear in the output of show configuration, so the rule rests on the targets alone. A switch that carries a target and never enabled the export is therefore silent, and a switch shipping its log somewhere else than to a syslog target is reported. The rule reads the targets and nothing else: whether a target is reachable, and whether the log filter attached to it forwards anything, is outside what a configuration can answer.

rules.title: The switch synchronizes its clock from no time server, neither SNTP nor NTP, so its log timestamps cannot be lined up with another device.
rules.remediation: Name a server and turn the client on: configure sntp-client primary with enable sntp-client, or configure ntp server add with enable ntp.
refs: ExtremeXOS v33.7.1 Command References, chapter Commands: enable sntp-client
ExtremeXOS v33.7.1 Command References, chapter Commands: configure sntp-client
ExtremeXOS v33.7.1 Command References, chapter Commands: enable ntp
ExtremeXOS v33.7.1 Command References, chapter Commands: configure ntp server add
rules.known_false_positives: 33.7.1 states no default for either client - the enable sntp-client and the disable sntp-client entry both read Default: N/A - so the rule infers no state and reads presence alone. Four commands silence it, each on its own: enable sntp-client, a configure sntp-client primary entry carrying a host, enable ntp, or a configure ntp server add entry carrying a host. The two clients are separate features of 33.7.1 and the rule does not judge which one a switch should use, only that it uses one; version 2 added the NTP half after a real dump was reported for holding its clock that way. A configuration naming only configure sntp-client secondary is still reported, because the rule accepts the primary entry alone, and so is one naming a server for a client that is turned off, because the dump does not carry the off state.

rules.title: Configuration management check: vlan-empty
rules.remediation: Review the identified object and the administrator policy; correct the finding before confirming a change.
refs: ExtremeXOS v33.7.1 Command References, chapter Commands: configure vlan add ports
rules.known_false_positives: Evaluates only visible configuration. Optional policy rules need an explicit operator policy. Unused objects are informational; absent evidence is not proof of a complete configuration.
